transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi, thank you. Well, what brought me in today is that I keep getting up in situations where I really should just stay seated. 

It happens a lot during staff meetings at the school, or even just sitting at dinner when everyone else is sitting down. I'll suddenly feel like I need to get up to refill my coffee, or go check a handout, or I'll just walk to the back of the room. And the thing is, none of it is ever really urgent. I just seem to have a hard time staying in my chair.
When did you first start having this difficulty staying seated?

Well, I think it's been noticeably harder to manage for about eight months now. That's right around when my youngest left for college. The house became a lot quieter, and... I don't know, ever since then, it's just been a lot more difficult to just sit still.
Did you experience this kind of restlessness or trouble sitting still when you were a child?

Yes, actually. Even as a young girl, it was an issue. I remember my old report cards usually said that I was a bright student, but that I just couldn't stay in my seat or wait my turn. 

My mother actually used to joke about it. She'd say that I had worn a path in the floor between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I even turned ten. So, yes, looking back, it's definitely something I struggled with as a child, too.
Do you often have difficulty sustaining your focus on tasks or activities?

No, not really. I don't usually have a problem focusing on my work or grading papers or anything like that. Once I'm actually doing a task, I can pay attention to it just fine. It's really just the sitting still part that gets to me.
